questions.q: If the feasible region of a linear programming problem with objective function $Z = ax + by$, is bounded, then which of the following is correct ?
options: (A) It will only have a maximum value.
(B) It will only have a minimum value.
(C) It will have both maximum and minimum values.
(D) It will have neither maximum nor minimum value.
questions.answer: It will have both maximum and minimum values.
keySteps: State that a continuous function on a bounded feasible region (compact set) always attains its maximum and minimum values — 1 mark

questions.q: The unit vector perpendicular to the vectors $\hat{i} - \hat{j}$ and $\hat{i} + \hat{j}$ is
keySteps: Compute the cross product of $(\hat{i} - \hat{j})$ and $(\hat{i} + \hat{j})$ as $2\hat{k}$ — 0.5 mark
Normalize the result to find the unit vector $\hat{k}$ — 0.5 mark

questions.q: If $\int_0^1 \frac{e^x}{1+x} dx = \alpha$, then $\int_0^1 \frac{e^x}{(1+x)^2} dx$ is equal to
keySteps: Use the property $\int e^x [f(x) + f'(x)] dx = e^x f(x)$ with $f(x) = \frac{1}{1+x}$ — 0.5 mark
Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to 1 to get $\alpha - \int_0^1 \frac{e^x}{(1+x)^2} dx = \frac{e}{2} - 1$ and solve for the required integral — 0.5 mark

questions.q: If $\int \frac{2^{\frac{1}{x}}}{x^2} dx = k \cdot 2^{\frac{1}{x}} + C$, then $k$ is equal to
keySteps: Substitute $t = 1/x$ so that $dt = -1/x^2 dx$ — 0.5 mark
Integrate $-2^t$ to get $-2^t/\log 2$ and identify $k = -1/\log 2$ — 0.5 mark

questions.q: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$, then $A^{-1}$ is
keySteps: Observe that $A$ is a diagonal matrix where $A^2 = I$ — 0.5 mark
Conclude $A^{-1} = A$ — 0.5 mark

questions.q: If $\begin{bmatrix} x+y & 3y \\ 3x & x+3 \\ \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 9 & 4x+y \\ x+6 & y \\ \end{bmatrix}$, then $(x-y) = ?$
keySteps: Equate corresponding elements to find $x = 3$ and $y = 6$ — 0.5 mark
Calculate $x - y = 3 - 6 = -3$ — 0.5 mark

questions.q: Let $M$ and $N$ be two events such that $P(M) = 0.6, P(N) = 0.2$ and $P(M|N) = 0.5$, then $P(M'/N')$ is
keySteps: Calculate $P(M \cap N) = P(M|N)P(N) = 0.1$ — 0.5 mark
Use De Morgan's law and $P(M'|N') = \frac{1 - P(M \cup N)}{1 - P(N)} = \frac{0.3}{0.8} = \frac{3}{8}$ — 0.5 mark

questions.q: Which of the following is not a homogeneous function of $x$ and $y$ ?
keySteps: Check homogeneity by substituting $(\lambda x, \lambda y)$ into each function — 0.5 mark
Identify that $\tan x - \sec y$ does not satisfy $f(\lambda x, \lambda y) = \lambda^n f(x, y)$ — 0.5 mark

questions.q: If $\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c} = \vec{0}$, $|\vec{a}| = \sqrt{37}$, $|\vec{b}| = 3$ and $|\vec{c}| = 4$, then angle between $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ is
keySteps: Use $\vec{b} + \vec{c} = -\vec{a}$ and square both sides: $|\vec{b}|^2 + |\vec{c}|^2 + 2\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c} = |\vec{a}|^2$ — 0.5 mark
Substitute values $9 + 16 + 24\cos \theta = 37$ to find $\cos \theta = 1/2$ and $\theta = \pi/3$ — 0.5 mark

questions.q: If $f(x) = |x| + |x-1|$, then which of the following is correct ?
options: (A) $f(x)$ is both continuous and differentiable, at $x=0$ and $x=1$.
(B) $f(x)$ is differentiable but not continuous, at $x=0$ and $x=1$.
(C) $f(x)$ is continuous but not differentiable, at $x=0$ and $x=1$.
(D) $f(x)$ is neither continuous nor differentiable, at $x=0$ and $x=1$.
questions.answer: $f(x)$ is continuous but not differentiable, at $x=0$ and $x=1$.
keySteps: State that the sum of continuous functions is continuous — 0.5 mark
Show that the derivative does not exist at the corner points $x=0$ and $x=1$ due to the absolute value terms — 0.5 mark

questions.q: A system of linear equations is represented as $AX = B$, where $A$ is coefficient matrix, $X$ is variable matrix and $B$ is the constant matrix. Then the system of equations is
options: (A) Consistent, if $|A| \neq 0$, solution is given by $X = BA^{-1}$.
(D) May or may not be consistent if $|A| = 0$ and $(\text{adj } A)B = 0$.
questions.answer: May or may not be consistent if $|A| = 0$ and $(\text{adj } A)B = 0$.
keySteps: Recall the criteria for consistency in a system of linear equations $AX=B$ — 1 mark

questions.q: The absolute maximum value of function $f(x) = x^3 - 3x + 2$ in $[0, 2]$ is :
keySteps: Find critical points by setting $f'(x) = 3x^2 - 3 = 0$, giving $x = 1$ in $[0, 2]$ — 0.5 mark
Compare $f(0)=2, f(1)=0, f(2)=4$ to find the absolute maximum — 0.5 mark

questions.q: The order and degree of differential function $\left[ 1 + \left( \frac{dy}{dx} \right)^2 \right]^5 = \frac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ are
keySteps: Identify the highest order derivative as $\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ (order 2) — 0.5 mark
Identify the power of the highest order derivative as 1 (degree 1) — 0.5 mark

questions.q: The graph of a trigonometric function is as shown. Which of the following will represent graph of its inverse ? [Main graph shows $y = \sin x$ for $x \in [-\pi/2, \pi/2]$]
keySteps: Identify the original graph as $y = \sin x$ on its principal domain — 0.5 mark
Recognize the graph of $y = \sin^{-1} x$ as its reflection in $y=x$ — 0.5 mark

questions.q: The corner points of the feasible region in graphical representation of a L.P.P. are $(2, 72), (15, 20)$ and $(40, 15)$. If $Z = 18x + 9y$ be the objective function, then
keySteps: Calculate $Z$ at each corner point: $Z(2, 72)=684, Z(15, 20)=450, Z(40, 15)=855$ — 0.5 mark
Identify the maximum and minimum values — 0.5 mark

questions.q: Let $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & -1 \\ -3 & 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}, B = \begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ -5 \\ -7 \end{bmatrix}, C = \begin{bmatrix} 9 & 8 & 7 \end{bmatrix}$, which of the following is defined ?
keySteps: Check matrix multiplication compatibility: $A(3\times3)B(3\times1)$ is defined — 0.5 mark
Check $AC(3\times3)(1\times3)$ and $BA(3\times1)(3\times3)$ are undefined — 0.5 mark

questions.q: If $A$ and $B$ are invertible matrices, then which of the following is not correct ?
keySteps: Identify that matrix inversion is not distributive over addition — 1 mark

questions.q: The area of the shaded region bounded by the curves $y^2 = x, x = 4$ and the $x$-axis is given by [Graph shows region in first quadrant]
keySteps: Express $y$ in terms of $x$ as $y = \sqrt{x}$ for the first quadrant — 0.5 mark
Set up the integral for area under the curve from $x=0$ to $x=4$ — 0.5 mark

questions.q: Assertion (A) : $f(x) = \begin{cases} 3x - 8, & x \le 5 \\ 2k, & x > 5 \end{cases}$ is continuous at $x = 5$ for $k = \frac{5}{2}$. \nReason (R) : For a function $f$ to be continuous at $x = a$, $\lim_{x \to a^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to a^+} f(x) = f(a)$.
options: (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and the Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
(B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
(C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
(D) Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.answer: (D) Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
keySteps: Check LHL and RHL at $x=5$: $LHL = 3(5)-8=7$, $RHL = 2k$ — 0.5 marks
For continuity $2k=7 \implies k=7/2$, so Assertion is false; Reason is the standard definition — 0.5 marks

questions.q: Assertion (A) : Let $Z$ be the set of integers. A function $f : Z \to Z$ defined as $f(x) = 3x - 5, \forall x \in Z$ is a bijective. \nReason (R) : A function is a bijective if it is both surjective and injective.
options: (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and the Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
(B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
(C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
(D) Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.answer: (D) Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
keySteps: Check surjectivity: $f(x)=0 \implies x=5/3 \notin Z$, so $f$ is not surjective and thus not bijective — 0.5 marks
Verify Reason: Bijective means both injective and surjective, which is true — 0.5 marks

questions.q: The diagonals of a parallelogram are given by $\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}$ and $\vec{b} = \hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - \hat{k}$. Find the area of the parallelogram.
keySteps: Compute the cross product of diagonals $\vec{a} \times \vec{b} = -2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}$ — 1 mark
Calculate the area using $\frac{1}{2} |\vec{a} \times \vec{b}| = \frac{\sqrt{4+9+49}}{2} = \frac{\sqrt{62}}{2}$ — 1 mark

questions.q: Find the values of 'a' for which $f(x) = \sqrt{3} \sin x - \cos x - 2ax + b$ is decreasing on $\mathbb{R}$.
keySteps: Find the derivative $f'(x) = \sqrt{3} \cos x + \sin x - 2a$ — 0.5 marks
Set the condition for decreasing function $f'(x) \le 0 \implies \sqrt{3} \cos x + \sin x \le 2a$ — 0.5 marks
Identify the maximum value of $\sqrt{3} \cos x + \sin x$ as $\sqrt{(\sqrt{3})^2 + 1^2} = 2$ — 0.5 marks
Solve $2 \le 2a$ to get $a \ge 1$ — 0.5 marks

questions.q: (a) Two friends while flying kites from different locations, find the strings of their kites crossing each other. The strings can be represented by vectors $\vec{a} = 3\hat{i} + \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b} = 2\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$. Determine the angle formed between the kite strings. Assume there is no slack in the strings.
questions.orAlternative: (b) Find a vector of magnitude 21 units in the direction opposite to that of $\vec{AB}$ where A and B are the points $A(2, 1, 3)$ and $B(8, -1, 0)$ respectively.
keySteps: Compute $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = 6 - 2 + 8 = 12$ — 0.5 marks
Compute magnitudes $|\vec{a}| = \sqrt{14}$ and $|\vec{b}| = \sqrt{24} = 2\sqrt{6}$ — 0.5 marks
Apply formula $\cos \theta = \frac{12}{\sqrt{14} \cdot 2\sqrt{6}} = \frac{3}{\sqrt{21}}$ — 0.5 marks
Final angle $\theta = \cos^{-1} \left( \frac{\sqrt{21}}{7} \right)$ — 0.5 marks

questions.q: Solve for $x$, $2 \tan^{-1} x + \sin^{-1} \left( \frac{2x}{1+x^2} \right) = \frac{4\pi}{3}$
keySteps: Use the identity $\sin^{-1} \left( \frac{2x}{1+x^2} \right) = 2 \tan^{-1} x$ (assuming principal branch) — 1 mark
Solve $4 \tan^{-1} x = \frac{4\pi}{3} \implies \tan^{-1} x = \frac{\pi}{3} \implies x = \sqrt{3}$ — 1 mark

questions.q: (a) Differentiate $2^{\cos^2 x}$ w.r.t $\cos^2 x$.
keySteps: Let $u = \cos^2 x$, then differentiate $2^u$ with respect to $u$ — 1 mark
Apply the formula $\frac{d}{du}(a^u) = a^u \log a$ to get $2^{\cos^2 x} \log 2$ — 1 mark

questions.q:
Solve the following linear programming problem graphically : 
Maximize $Z = 8x + 9y$ 
Subject to the constraints : 
$2x + 3y \le 6$ 
$3x - 2y \le 6$ 
$y \le 1$ 
$x \ge 0, y \ge 0$
keySteps: Plot the constraints and identify the feasible region — 1 mark
Evaluate $Z$ at corner points and find the maximum value — 1 mark

questions.q: (a) Find : $\int \frac{2x - 1}{(x - 1)(x + 2)(x - 3)} dx$
keySteps: Decompose into partial fractions: $\frac{2x-1}{(x-1)(x+2)(x-3)} = \frac{-1/6}{x-1} + \frac{-1/3}{x+2} + \frac{1/2}{x-3}$ — 1.5 marks
Integrate each term to get the final logarithmic expression — 1.5 marks

questions.q: A spherical medicine ball when dropped in water dissolves in such a way that the rate of decrease of volume at any instant is proportional to its surface area. Calculate the rate of decrease of its radius.
questions.answer: The rate of decrease of radius is constant.
keySteps: Write $\frac{dV}{dt} = -k S$ where $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$ and $S = 4\pi r^2$ — 1 mark
Substitute derivatives: $4\pi r^2 \frac{dr}{dt} = -k (4\pi r^2)$ — 1 mark
Simplify to find $\frac{dr}{dt} = -k$, showing the rate is constant — 1 mark

questions.q: Sketch the graph of $y = |x + 3|$ and find the area of the region enclosed by the curve, $x$-axis, between $x = -6$ and $x = 0$, using integration.
keySteps: Sketch the V-shaped graph of $y = |x+3|$ with vertex at $(-3, 0)$ — 1 mark
Set up the integral: $\int_{-6}^{-3} -(x+3) dx + \int_{-3}^0 (x+3) dx$ — 1 mark
Calculate the area: $4.5 + 4.5 = 9$ — 1 mark

questions.q: (a) Verify that lines given by $\vec{r} = (1 - \lambda)\hat{i} + (\lambda - 2)\hat{j} + (3 - 2\lambda)\hat{k}$ and $\vec{r} = (\mu + 1)\hat{i} + (2\mu - 1)\hat{j} - (2\mu + 1)\hat{k}$ are skew lines. Hence, find shortest distance between the lines.
questions.orAlternative: (b) During a cricket match, the position of the bowler, the wicket keeper and the leg slip fielder are in a line given by $\vec{B} = 2\hat{i} + 8\hat{j}$, $\vec{W} = 6\hat{i} + 12\hat{j}$ and $\vec{F} = 12\hat{i} + 18\hat{j}$ respectively. Calculate the ratio in which the wicketkeeper divides the line segment joining the bowler and the leg slip fielder.
keySteps: Identify $\vec{a}_1, \vec{b}_1, \vec{a}_2, \vec{b}_2$ from the line equations — 0.5 marks
Compute $(\vec{a}_2 - \vec{a}_1) \cdot (\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2) = 8 \neq 0$, verifying lines are skew — 1 mark
Calculate $|\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2| = \sqrt{29}$ and apply SD formula — 1.5 marks

questions.q:
(a) The probability distribution for the number of students being absent in a class on a Saturday is as follows : 
 egin{tabular}{|l|c|c|c|c|} \hline X & 0 & 2 & 4 & 5 \ \hline P(X) & p & 2p & 3p & p \ \hline \end{tabular} 
Where X is the number of students absent. 
(i) Calculate p. 
(ii) Calculate the mean of the number of absent students on Saturday.
questions.orAlternative: (b) For the vacancy advertised in the newspaper, 3000 candidates submitted their applications. From the data it was revealed that two third of the total applicants were females and other were males. The selection for the job was done through a written test. The performance of the applicants indicates that the probability of a male getting a distinction in written test is 0.4 and that a female getting a distinction is 0.35. Find the probability that the candidate chosen at random will have a distinction in the written test.
keySteps: Use $\sum P(X) = 1 \implies 7p = 1 \implies p = 1/7$ — 1 mark
Apply mean formula $E(X) = \sum X P(X) = 0(p) + 2(2p) + 4(3p) + 5(p)$ — 1 mark
Calculate Mean $= 21p = 21(1/7) = 3$ — 1 mark

questions.q: A school wants to allocate students into three clubs : Sports, Music and Drama, under following conditions : \n\begin{itemize} \item The number of students in Sports club should be equal to the sum of the number of students in Music and Drama club. \item The number of students in Music club should be 20 more than half the number of students in Sports club. \item The total number of students to be allocated in all three clubs are 180. \end{itemize} \nFind the number of students allocated to different clubs, using matrix method.
keySteps: Formulate equations: $x-y-z=0, -x+2y=40, x+y+z=180$ — 1 mark
Write in matrix form $AX=B$ and find $|A|=4$ — 1 mark
Compute $adj(A)$ and $A^{-1}$ — 2 marks
Solve $X = A^{-1}B$ to get $x=90, y=65, z=25$ — 1 mark

questions.q: Find : $\int \sin^{-1} \sqrt{\frac{x}{a + x}} dx$.
keySteps: Substitute $x = a \tan^2 \theta$, $dx = 2a \tan \theta \sec^2 \theta d\theta$ — 1 mark
Simplify integral to $\int \theta \cdot 2a \tan \theta \sec^2 \theta d\theta$ — 1 mark
Integrate by parts to get $a \theta \tan^2 \theta - a(\tan \theta - \theta) + C$ — 2 marks
Back-substitute $\theta = \tan^{-1} \sqrt{x/a}$ to get final answer — 1 mark

questions.q: (a) If $\sqrt{1 - x^2} + \sqrt{1 - y^2} = a(x - y)$, then prove that $\frac{dy}{dx} = \sqrt{\frac{1 - y^2}{1 - x^2}}$.
questions.orAlternative: (b) If $x = a \left( \cos \theta + \log \tan \frac{\theta}{2} \right)$ and $y = a \sin \theta$, then find $\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ at $\theta = \frac{\pi}{4}$.
keySteps: (a) Substitute $x = \sin \alpha, y = \sin \beta$ and simplify to $\sin^{-1} x - \sin^{-1} y = 2 \cot^{-1} a$ — 2 marks
Differentiate both sides with respect to $x$ — 2 marks
Obtain the final expression $\frac{dy}{dx} = \sqrt{\frac{1 - y^2}{1 - x^2}}$ — 1 mark
OR (b) Find $\frac{dx}{d\theta} = a \frac{\cos^2 \theta}{\sin \theta}$ and $\frac{dy}{d\theta} = a \cos \theta$ — 2 marks
Find $\frac{dy}{dx} = \tan \theta$ — 1 mark
Find $\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \frac{\sin \theta}{a \cos^4 \theta}$ — 1.5 marks
Evaluate at $\theta = \frac{\pi}{4}$ to get $\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{a}$ — 0.5 marks

questions.q: (a) Find the image A' of the point $A(1, 6, 3)$ in the line $\frac{x}{1} = \frac{y - 1}{2} = \frac{z - 2}{3}$. Also, find the equation of the line joining A and A'.
questions.orAlternative: (b) Find a point P on the line $\frac{x + 5}{1} = \frac{y + 3}{4} = \frac{z - 6}{-9}$ such that its distance from point $Q(2, 4, -1)$ is 7 units. Also, find the equation of line joining P and Q.
keySteps: (a) Write general point $P(\lambda, 2\lambda+1, 3\lambda+2)$ and use $\vec{AP} \cdot \vec{d} = 0$ to find $\lambda = 1$ — 2 marks
Find foot of perpendicular $P(1, 3, 5)$ and image $A'(1, 0, 7)$ — 2 marks
Find equation of line $AA'$: $\frac{x-1}{0} = \frac{y-6}{-3} = \frac{z-3}{2}$ — 1 mark
OR (b) Write general point $P(\lambda-5, 4\lambda-3, -9\lambda+6)$ and set up $PQ^2 = 49$ — 2 marks
Solve for $\lambda = 1$ and find point $P(-4, 1, -3)$ — 2 marks
Find equation of line $PQ$: $\frac{x-2}{6} = \frac{y-4}{3} = \frac{z+1}{2}$ — 1 mark

questions.q:
A class-room teacher is keen to assess the learning of her students the concept of "relations" taught to them. She writes the following five relations each defined on the set $A = \{1, 2, 3\}$ : 
$R_1 = \{(2, 3), (3, 2)\}$ 
$R_2 = \{(1, 2), (1, 3), (3, 2)\}$ 
$R_3 = \{(1, 2), (2, 1), (1, 1)\}$ 
$R_4 = \{(1, 1), (1, 2), (3, 3), (2, 2)\}$ 
$R_5 = \{(1, 1), (1, 2), (3, 3), (2, 2), (2, 1), (2, 3), (3, 2)\}$ 
The students are asked to answer the following questions about the above relations :

parts.q: Identify the relation which is reflexive, transitive but not symmetric.
Identify the relation which is reflexive and symmetric but not transitive.
(a) Identify the relations which are symmetric but neither reflexive nor transitive.

questions.orAlternative: (iii) (b) What pairs should be added to the relation $R_2$ to make it an equivalence relation ?

questions.q: A bank offers loan to its customers on different types of interest namely, fixed rate, floating rate and variable rate. From the past data with the bank, it is known that a customer avails loan on fixed rate, floating rate or variable rate with probabilities 10%, 20% and 70% respectively. A customer after availing loan can pay the loan or default on loan repayment. The bank data suggests that the probability that a person defaults on loan after availing it at fixed rate, floating rate and variable rate is 5%, 3% and 1% respectively. \nBased on the above information, answer the following :

parts.q: What is the probability that a customer after availing the loan will default on the loan repayment ?
A customer after availing the loan, defaults on loan repayment. What is the probability that he availed the loan at a variable rate of interest ?

keySteps: (i) Use Total Probability Theorem: $P(D) = (0.1)(0.05) + (0.2)(0.03) + (0.7)(0.01)$ — 1 mark
Calculate $P(D) = 0.018$ — 1 mark
(ii) Use Bayes' Theorem: $P(V|D) = \frac{P(V)P(D|V)}{P(D)} = \frac{0.007}{0.018}$ — 1 mark
Calculate $P(V|D) = \frac{7}{18}$ — 1 mark

questions.q: A technical company is designing a rectangular solar panel installation on a roof using 300 metres of boundary material. The design includes a partition running parallel to one of the sides dividing the area (roof) into two sections. \nLet the length of the side perpendicular to the partition be $x$ metres and with parallel to the partition be $y$ metres. \nBased on this information, answer the following questions :

parts.q: Write the equation for the total boundary material used in the boundary and parallel to the partition in terms of $x$ and $y$.
Write the area of the solar panel as a function of $x$.
(a) Find the critical points of the area function. Use second derivative test to determine critical points at the maximum area. Also, find the maximum area.

questions.orAlternative: (iii) (b) Using first derivative test, calculate the maximum area the company can enclose with the 300 metres of boundary material, considering the parallel partition.
keySteps: (i) Write boundary equation $2x + 3y = 300$ — 1 mark
(ii) Express area $A = xy$ as $A(x) = x(100 - \frac{2}{3}x) = 100x - \frac{2}{3}x^2$ — 1 mark
(iii) Find critical point $A'(x) = 100 - \frac{4}{3}x = 0 \implies x = 75$ — 1 mark
Verify maxima using derivative test and calculate $A(75) = 3750 \text{ m}^2$ — 1 mark
